title: WhatsApp Chat System: Complete Architecture
description: Design a WhatsApp-scale instant messaging system with WebSockets, E2EE, offline queuing, and media delivery.

data.text: Design a WhatsApp-scale instant messaging system supporting 2 billion users exchanging 100 billion messages per day. The system must guarantee message delivery with receipts (sent ✓, delivered ✓✓, read ✓✓ blue), show real-time presence and typing indicators, support group chats up to 1024 participants, deliver media files (photos, videos, voice notes), enable end-to-end encryption, and operate reliably across poor network conditions with offline queuing.

terms.definition: Persistent full-duplex TCP connection enabling server-push without polling overhead.
Lightweight messaging protocols; MQTT is preferred for mobile due to minimal overhead on unreliable networks.
Process of delivering one message to multiple recipients (e.g., broadcasting to a group chat of 1024).
End-to-end encryption protocol using Double Ratchet Algorithm for perfect forward secrecy.
Component tracking online/offline/typing status, broadcasting changes to relevant users.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Send 1:1 and group text messages with delivery receipts (sent, delivered, read)
Share media (photos, videos up to 2GB, voice notes, documents) with thumbnails
Real-time presence: online, offline with last-seen timestamp, typing indicator
Group chats up to 1024 participants with admin controls and invite links
End-to-end encryption using Signal Protocol (server sees only ciphertext)
Push notifications (FCM / APNs) when app is backgrounded
Offline message queue: store pending messages and sync on reconnect
Voice and video calls (WebRTC, separate from message path)

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Message delivery latency: <100ms P95 for online users
2 billion registered users; 500 million daily active users
Media storage: petabytes scale, deduplicated by content hash
Horizontal scaling; no single point of failure
Multi-region active-active with geo-partitioned user data

data.caption: Message delivery sequence: sender → connection server → message router → fan-out → recipient (online) or offline queue → push notification
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Alice as 📱 Alice (Sender)
    participant CS_A as 🖥️ Conn Server A
    participant Router as 📨 Message Router
    participant Fanout as 📡 Fan-out
    participant Kafka as 📬 Kafka
    participant Session as 📋 Session Registry
    participant CS_B as 🖥️ Conn Server B
    participant Bob as 📱 Bob (Recipient)
    participant Queue as 📬 Offline Queue
    participant FCM as 🔔 FCM/APNs

    Alice->>CS_A: Send Message (E2E encrypted payload)
    CS_A->>Router: Route message (idempotency_key)
    Router->>Kafka: Publish message event
    Kafka->>Fanout: Consume event
    Fanout->>Session: Lookup Bob's connection server
    alt Bob is Online
        Session-->>Fanout: CS_B (Bob connected)
        Fanout->>CS_B: Push message to Bob's WS
        CS_B->>Bob: Deliver message (✓✓ delivered)
        Bob->>CS_B: Send read receipt
        CS_B->>CS_A: Forward read receipt
        CS_A->>Alice: ✓✓ blue (read)
    else Bob is Offline
        Session-->>Fanout: Not connected
        Fanout->>Queue: Enqueue for Bob
        Fanout->>FCM: Trigger push notification
        FCM->>Bob: Push notification
        Bob->>CS_B: Reconnect, request pending messages
        CS_B->>Queue: Drain Bob's queue
        Queue-->>CS_B: Deliver queued messages
        CS_B->>Bob: Deliver messages (✓✓ delivered)
    end

data.title: Group Fan-out Challenge
data.text: A group with 1024 members receiving 1 message requires delivering to up to 1024 different connection servers. At 1M messages/day in a large group, this is 1 billion individual deliveries. WhatsApp solves this with a two-tier fan-out: immediate push to online members, batch delivery to offline members via a single queue drain on reconnect.

items.question: How does end-to-end encryption work without server seeing messages?
items.answer: Signal Protocol uses Curve25519 for key exchange and AES-256-GCM for encryption. Each session has independent keys via the Double Ratchet Algorithm. The server stores only public keys and encrypted ciphertext — it cannot decrypt messages even with a court order.

items.question: How do you guarantee exactly-once delivery while at scale?
items.answer: WhatsApp uses at-least-once delivery with client-side deduplication. Each message carries a UUID idempotency key. The client checks its local DB before displaying, silently dropping duplicates. This is simpler and more reliable than exactly-once at the broker level.

items.question: How is presence (online/offline) handled at 2B users?
items.answer: Clients send heartbeats every 30 seconds over the persistent WebSocket. Connection servers update a Redis TTL key. When the TTL expires (60s), the user is marked offline. Presence broadcasts are limited to mutual contacts using a subscription model to avoid fan-out storms.

items.question: How to handle media deduplication across billions of files?
items.answer: SHA-256 hash the media client-side before upload. If the hash already exists in the object store, skip the upload entirely (content-addressed storage). This drastically reduces storage — viral media (memes, videos) shared by millions is stored only once.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Persistent WebSocket connections per user eliminate polling overhead at scale
Session registry (Redis) maps userId → connection server enabling cross-server delivery
Separate offline queue ensures at-least-once delivery even through network outages
E2E encryption means the server stores only ciphertext; key exchange uses public key cryptography only
Media deduplication via content hashing saves petabytes of storage for viral content
data.takeaway: WhatsApp's architecture is fundamentally about maintaining billion concurrent connections efficiently, routing messages to the right connection server in milliseconds, and guaranteeing delivery through robust offline queuing and push notifications.
